questions.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-3 \\ y=5t \\ z=-2\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
questions.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5t \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

questions.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=t-1 \\ y=-t+1 \\ z=-t-1\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}t-1 \\ -t+1 \\ -t-1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}t \\ -t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-1,1,-1)$   and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083350/assets/58076d96d149ff4521103fd15c7187bc1a58595ab20f28be92be0f79385aee61.png)

Find the parametric equations of the line shown in the figure above.
questions.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the points $P(-1,1,4)$ and $Q(3,-2,2).$ Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$,  as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -3t \\ -2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1+4t \\ 1-3t \\ 4-2t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Therefore, the parametric equations are:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1+4t \\ y=1-3t \\ z=4-2t\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Fill in the missing parts in the parametric equations below that describe all the points on the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ},$ where $P(4,-1,7)$ and $Q(-6,5,0).$

| $x=$ | {{field-1}} | $t\in [0,$ {{field-2}} $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y=$ | {{field-3}} |  |
| $z=$ | $7-7t$ |  |
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the line passing through the given points. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 6 \\ -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 6 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-10t \\ 6t \\ -7t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4-10t \\ -1+6t \\ 7-7t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

To get the equations for the line segment, we take only $t\in [0,1].$ Notice that substitution of $t=0$ in the above equation gives the coordinates of $P$ and substitution of $t=1$ gives the coordinates of $Q.$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ are the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=4-10t \\ y=-1+6t \\ z=7-7t\end{aligned}\,\,t\in [0,1]
$$

\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 10 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ 10t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-4+4t \\ -2+10t \\ 4-t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

To get the equations for the line segment, we take only $t\in [0,1].$ Notice that substitution of $t=0$ in the above equation gives the coordinates of $P$ and substitution of $t=1$ gives the coordinates of $Q.$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ are the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-4+4t \\ y=-2+10t \\ z=4-t\end{aligned}\,\,t\in [0,1]
$$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the points $P(3,3,-5)$ and $Q(1,0,-1)$. Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ -5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ -5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2t \\ -3t \\ 4t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3-2t \\ 3-3t \\ -5+4t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3-2t \\ y=3-3t \\ z=-5+4t\end{aligned}
$$
